subject: effect of rescaling covariate on model outputs

messages.author: 863a0481c01d0ecd
messages.subject: effect of rescaling covariate on model outputs
parts:
Dear INLA friends,

Would you explain me why rescaling a covariate (x) is giving me comparable modeling outputs when I assume a linear effect on the response (y) but NOT when I assume a nonlinear effect?

I am assessing this model:

mod=inla(formula, data=Data123,family='nbinomial, control.fixed=list(prec.intercept=0.1), control.compute=list(E=weights)

assuming these linear vs. non-linear effects of x on y:

formula= y ~ x+ f(id, model = "bym", graph = g) + f(year.struct, 
    model = "ar1") + f(year, model = "iid")

formula= y ~  f(inla.group(x), model="rw2") + f(id, model = "bym", graph = g) + f(year.struct,  model = "ar1") + f(year, model = "iid")

For the linear effect, both DIC and mean/sd of the hyper parameter of x are similar regardless of the scale of x (2747, -8.4 respectively)

However rescaling for the non-linear effect produces a worse model  (DIC= 2748 vs 2703), and a non-sensitive effect of x (mean/sd of hyperparameter =0.97 vs 1.76).


The transformation I am making for x is:
 x<-(x-mean(x))/(2*sd(x))

Thanks for any help.

Victor.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] effect of rescaling covariate on model outputs
parts:
On Thu, 2015-04-16 at 09:42 -0700, Víctor Hugo Gutiérrez Vélez wrote:

>
> Would you explain me why rescaling a covariate (x) is giving me
> comparable modeling outputs when I assume a linear effect on the
> response (y) but NOT when I assume a nonlinear effect?

Hi,

this is because the prior is kept fixed, hence rescaling x implicitely
change the prior.

You'll see his effect also in the fixed-effects, looking at the stdev

> inla(y~x, data=data.frame(y=0,x=1))$summary.fixed["x","sd"]
[1] 31.62277669
> inla(y~x, data=data.frame(y=0,x=1111111))$summary.fixed["x","sd"]
[1] 0.2453530524


so you need to adjust control.fixed=list(prec=...) so that the
'effective' prior is the same.

Using 'rw2', the issue is the same, but there is more to it.

f(x, model="rw2")

and

xx = x * 1000
f(xx, model="rw2")

would behave VERY different. It is the same issue as above, additional
to the behaviour of RW2 which also depends on the length(x). This is
discussed in detail in this tutorial,

http://www.r-inla.org/examples/tutorials/tutorial-on-option-scale-model

arguing for that its best to use

f(xx, model="rw2", scale=TRUE)

which will rescale the model so that using 'x' and 'xx' is the same.

Best
H
